“What are you doing?” he asked, his voice a little breathless. 

“Just… clearing,” I said, my voice rougher than I intended. “Trying to make it look a bit less… overgrown.”  I paused, watching him. "You seem to like this place."

It allows us to believe that our successes are due to our own merit our brilliance our hard work while our failures are simply unfortunate accidents or miscalculations. But the quote elevates them to something far more profound. It suggests that God is subtly manipulating these coincidences to maintain a veil of mystery.

Similarly, these seemingly random occurrences are connected through a complex web of cause and effect that we don't fully grasp. God is the silent observer of this web allowing it to continue undisturbed.

The anonymity aspect is particularly compelling. It implies a lack of direct involvement. We attribute events to chance or luck or even to the sheer randomness of existence.
